records.proposal: You want most of the waiting records cleared without a separate yes from you for each. Asked how (context, calibration, or both), you answered "Both" in Claude Code's question dialog. (1) Project context settles the clearly safe records now: a requirement whose linked code exists, whose covering tests pass, and that an independent model finds consistent with everything you confirmed and with the code, settles without your words. It is labelled "settled by context", listed for you once, and undoable in one step. (2) In parallel, the mod shows trial cards so your Accept/Reject answers calibrate JEV; once calibration passes, settling from your words (SP8) takes over. (3) Older records' quotes are found in past session transcripts by a JEV, Sonnet, Opus cascade and shown on their cards; your press is the proof, the transcript alone is not.

A proposed requirement settles by context when all hold: every implemented_by link is current and its code exists; its covering tests ran and passed on the current tree; an independent model (not the coding agent) judges it consistent with every owner-confirmed record and with the linked code; it is not a decision, an intent, an escalated set member, or an edit of an owner-confirmed record. The approval is logged as 'by: context' with the tests, the model and its verdict, listed to the owner once, and revocable in one step. Losing any condition makes it proposed again.

For a record whose quote is not in a hook-logged prompt, JEV pairs it with the most likely owner message in past session transcripts, Sonnet picks the exact span, and Opus examines records whose words do not support them; the found words, their date and session are shown on the record's card. The exact-match check stays a text comparison. A transcript match alone never confirms; the owner's press or logged words do.

A trial batch reaches the owner in the mod with Yes and No per record. Each press is a labelled owner answer: Yes confirms the record (by owner, via button, label yes), No is a capture-error rejection that calibration counts as a real 'no'; the No marks plumb's reading wrong and the record stays (the owner is not told it was dropped, the agent is told not to remove or rewrite it). A record answered in its batch is not offered again (trial batches only; every other card keeps all its questions); each button names its record's offer, so a press from an out-of-date draw cannot land on another record; the calibration reruns from the logged scores once the batch is answered (SR-106), counting every press of it; a batch left open is not asked again in another batch until its record changes, and then it comes back.
